findings.claim: `tprod_nonneg` asks for `[L.NeBot]`, but the statement is true without it. It is also the only total `tprod`/`tsum` bound in this file that asks for it. Its neighbours `one_le_tprod` (whose additive version is `tsum_nonneg`), `tprod_le_one` and `tprod_le_of_prod_le'` drop `L.NeBot` and handle the `¬ L.NeBot` case with `tprod_bot` plus a `finprod` argument. The same argument works under this lemma's hypotheses: `finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf` only needs `ZeroLEOneClass`, `Preorder` and `PosMulMono`. As written, any caller that is generic in `L` cannot use the lemma unless it also carries `[L.NeBot]`. One example is a `tprod` counterpart of the `evalTsum` positivity extension at the end of this file, which calls `tsum_nonneg` for an arbitrary `$L` without finding a `NeBot` instance. Separately, the multipliable branch repeats the proof of the `HasProd.nonneg` added just above (`le_hasProd_of_le_prod` is just `ge_of_tendsto'`) instead of calling it. `one_le_tprod` calls `hg.hasProd.one_le h` at the same point.
findings.requested_change:
Remove `[L.NeBot]` from `tprod_nonneg`, keep it on `HasProd.nonneg`, and follow the structure of `one_le_tprod`:
```
theorem tprod_nonneg [CommMonoidWithZero α] [TopologicalSpace α] [Preorder α] [ZeroLEOneClass α]
    [PosMulMono α] [ClosedIciTopology α] {f : ι → α} (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) :
    0 ≤ ∏'[L] x, f x := by
  by_cases h : Multipliable f L
  · by_cases hL : L.NeBot
    · exact h.hasProd.nonneg hf
    · simp only [tprod_bot hL]
      exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf
  · simp [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]
```

review_notes: Packet only, no Mathlib checkout, so nothing here was compiled. Compared the new pair against the non-strict pair `HasProd.one_le`/`one_le_tprod` and the strict `Multipliable.one_lt_tprod`/`hasProd_lt`. Keeping `HasProd.nonneg` is justified: `ClosedIciTopology` does not give T2, so a caller with `HasProd f a L` cannot reduce to `tprod_nonneg` via `HasProd.tprod_eq`, and the non-strict neighbour has the same HasProd/tprod split. Did not ask for a strict `HasProd.pos`/`tprod_pos`: the analogy breaks because positive factors can have product 0 (in ℝ, `HasProd (fun _ ↦ 1/2) 0`), so it would need different hypotheses. Also did not ask for `Multipliable.tprod_nonneg`, since `tprod_nonneg` needs no multipliability. Did not file `Preorder` vs `PartialOrder`, missing docstrings (neighbours have none), a shared `variable` line, or a positivity extension for `tprod`: these are preferences or new scope. The one finding comes from the file's own handling of `¬ L.NeBot` in `one_le_tprod`/`tprod_le_one`/`tprod_le_of_prod_le'`. The reuse of `HasProd.nonneg` is folded into it, since the proof gets rewritten anyway.
